label: Понимать
description: A 10-sentence conjugation card for понимать (to understand).

missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person singular present. 'Понимаю' is the standard я-form with the -ю ending. 'Русский язык' is the accusative direct object of imperfective понимать.
Strategic focus: Second-person singular present. 'Понимаешь' shows the -ешь ending of the first conjugation. The clause 'что я говорю' serves as the object of understanding.
Strategic focus: Third-person singular present. 'Понимает' is the он-form ending in -ет, here negated. 'Эту задачу' is the accusative object.

missions.phrase: Мы понимаем друг друга без слов.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: First-person plural present. 'Понимаем' shows the мы-ending -ем. 'Друг друга' is the reciprocal object, 'without words' a fixed phrase.
Strategic focus: Third-person plural present. 'Понимают' completes the present ladder with the -ют ending. 'Все наши проблемы' is the plural accusative object.

missions.phrase: Раньше я не понимал этого правила.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Masculine past tense. 'Понимал' is the masculine singular past of imperfective понимать. With negation the object 'этого правила' shifts to the genitive.
Strategic focus: Feminine past tense. 'Понимала' adds the feminine -а ending. The imperfective stresses an ongoing capacity; 'мои чувства' is the plural accusative object.
Strategic focus: Plural past tense. 'Понимали' is the plural past ending in -и. 'Этот урок' is the accusative object, and 'уже' marks accomplished comprehension.

missions.phrase: Завтра ты будешь лучше понимать материал.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Imperfective compound future. 'Будешь понимать' joins 'будешь' with the infinitive; понимать is imperfective, so the future is built periphrastically. The perfective partner is понять.

missions.phrase: Старайся понимать, а не просто слушать.
missions.fullAnalysis: Strategic focus: Infinitive use after a verb. 'Старайся' governs the bare infinitive 'понимать'. Pairing it with 'слушать' contrasts active understanding with mere listening.
